title: Full-Body Home Workout Plan — Zero Equipment
description: No gym membership? No problem. This complete home workout plan uses only bodyweight exercises to build strength, cardio, and flexibility — no equipment required.
author: Jake Reynolds

content.text: Your bodyweight is one of the most versatile training tools available. Push-ups, squats, lunges, planks, and pull-ups (using a door frame bar) can build significant muscle and cardiovascular fitness without any equipment.

items: Tuesday: Pull (inverted rows, pull-ups, face pulls with band)
Friday: Core & cardio (planks, mountain climbers, HIIT)

content.text: Add a resistance band set to dramatically increase exercise variety and difficulty at home — they are inexpensive and highly effective for upper body and glute work.

items.question: Can bodyweight training build real muscle?
items.answer: Yes. Bodyweight training can build substantial muscle, especially in the chest, triceps, shoulders, back, and legs. The key is progressive overload: increasing reps, slowing tempo, adding pauses, or progressing to harder variations (e.g. archer push-ups, pistol squats).

items.question: How long should a home workout be?
items.answer: Quality over quantity. A focused 25–45 minute session with minimal rest between exercises is more effective than an hour of unfocused training. You can achieve excellent results in 30 minutes with consistent effort.
